definition: The dotting test, also called the Serial Dotting Test, is a psychometric task included in the five-test porto-systemic encephalopathy battery that makes up the Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score. In this battery, it is used to help assess functions such as psychomotor speed, attention, and executive functioning.

reasons: The packet supports that the Serial Dotting Test is one of five psychometrical tests in the porto-systemic encephalopathy battery/PHES and that the battery assesses psychomotor retardation, attention deficit, and executive functions, but it does not specifically support the phrasing "psychomotor speed."

The definition is slightly over-specific by presenting the test as used to assess named cognitive domains in general, rather than limiting itself to the packet's wording about the PHES battery and its associated functions.
The packet mentions “Serial Dotting Test (SDT)” as part of the PHES battery, but it does not state that “dotting test” is also called “Serial Dotting Test.”
The packet says the tests “assess psychomotor retardation, attention deficit and executive functions,” whereas the definition claims “psychomotor speed.”
